title.narrative: World Bank Umbrella Facility for Trade
World Bank Umbrella Facility for Trade

description.narrative:
Nytt stöd till Världsbanksgruppens nya övergripande handelsfond, "Umbrella Facility for Trade" (UF-Trade). UF-Trade avser ersätta tidigare multigivarfonder utifrån en heltäckande handelsstrategi och ett sammanhängande resultatramverk.
Världsbanksgruppen med sitt mandat och stora kapacitet har möjlighet att ta ett helhetsgrepp kring handelsrelaterat utvecklingssamarbete. Genom policypåverkan, analyser, implementering samt finansiering har de förutsättningar som ingen annan aktör har.
UF-Trade bygger fortsatt på Världsbanksgruppens handelsstrategi och dess tematiska områden. Dessa är: i) konkurrenskraft och diversifiering; ii) handelsprocedurer, logistik och handelsfinansiering; iii) stöd för marknadstillträde och internationellt handelssamarbete; samt iv) hantering av chocker och stärkt inkluderande fattigdomsminskning. Utöver dessa har globala värdekedjor, regional integration och tjänstehandel identifierats som högprioriterade områden. Dessa liksom ett ökat fokus på bland annat jämställdhetsfrågor utgör ett tematiskt fönster som fördelas enligt:
- Regionala och nationella insatser - "just-in-time" för hastigt uppkomna behov - globala frågor såsom forskning, påverkansarbete och framtagandet av olika verktyg
Världsbanksgruppen har presenterat ett förslag på arbetsområden och aktiviteter under sex år med en totalt önskad budget på 180 miljoner USD. Svenskt stöd till UF-Trade föreslås med 90 miljoner SEK för initialt tre år. För de tre första åren är finansiering på ungefär 45-50 miljoner USD utlovade av Sverige, Nederländerna, Storbritannien, Schweiz och Norge vilket innebär att UF-Trade idag är underfinansierat gentemot önskad budget. Finansieringen för de avslutande tre åren kan vara avhängigt ytterligare givare samt resultat under de första åren.
Medlen ska fördelas på olika "kuvert" eller finansieringsfönster enligt följande fördelning:
1. Regionalt och nationellt arbete som kommer innebära majoriteten av aktiviteter beräknas erhålla 65% av tillgängliga medel. 2. Globala frågor och insatser relaterat till forskning, påverkansarbete globalt samt metod- och verktygsutveckling får 30% av tillgängliga medel. 3. Det sista fönstret som benämns "just-in-time" ger utrymme för hastigt uppkomna behov och till det avsätts högst 5% av budgeten.
Givarna har också kommit överens med Banken att 60% av tillgängliga medel ska fokuseras på Afrika söder om Sahara och andra låginkomstländer.
Då den övergripande budgeten utgör en grund för projekt och programprioriteringar finns ingen detaljerad budget för hela fonden vilket är normalt för en trust fund på exempelvis Världsbanken. Däremot finns det kriterier och tematiska prioriteringar för vad medlen får användas till. Majoriteten av pengarna går till analytiskt arbete i form av studier och behovsanalyser, forskning, utveckling av verktyg och indikatorer. Det sker som nämnts på nationell, regional och global nivå där användandet kan vara normativt eller bidra till global dialog eller som underlag för vidare implementering av större gåvo eller låneprojekt. Världsbanksgruppens administrationskostnad baseras på en standard på 17%.
Inom UF-Trade kommer ett fönster finansiera aktiviteter under Världbanksgruppens "Trade Facilitation Support Program" (TFSP). TFSP:s funktion är att hjälpa utvecklingsländer med implementeringen av WTO:s Trade Facilitation Agreement. Det innebär att förenkla tull- och handelsprocedurer för att sänka transport- och transaktionskostnader i gränsöverskridande handel vilket utgör ett stort bekymmer för många utvecklingsländer. Utöver ovan nämnda givare bidrar även USA, Kanada och EU till TFSP som i dagsläget har en total budget på 36 MUSD. Sverige föreslår att 15 MSEK av det totala stödet till UF-Trade öronmärks till TFSP.
Mot bakgrund att den inte finns en detaljerad budget i detta skedde anser Sida ändå att budgeten framstår som rimlig och berättigad samt att det finns en systematik för hanteringen av budgetfrågor både på projektnivå och aggregerad nivå. Givarna har också möjlighet att påverka styrningen av budgeten i dialog med Världsbanksgruppen.
Sida och Världbanksgruppen avser använda avtalsmallen för multigivarfonder som förhandlades med Världsbanken inom CGOP, med justeringar för att innefatta International Finance Corporation IFC. Både Världsbanken och IFC skriver under avtalet.

Support to World Bank Umbrella Trust Fund for Trade. Will replace existing trust funds under the World Bank Trade Strategy and with one integrated results framework.
The World Bank Group, with its mandate and large capacity, has the opportunity to take a comprehensive approach to trade-related development cooperation. Through policy influence, analyses, implementation and financing, they have conditions that no other actor has.
UF-Trade continues to build on the World Bank Group's trade strategy and its thematic areas. These are: i) competitiveness and diversification; ii) trade procedures, logistics and trade finance; iii) support for market access and international trade cooperation; and iv) management of shocks and strengthened inclusive poverty reduction. In addition to these, global value chains, regional integration and trade in services have been identified as high priority areas. These, as well as an increased focus on, among other things, gender equality issues constitute a thematic window which is distributed according to:
- Regional and national efforts - "just-in-time" for rapidly arising needs - global issues such as research, advocacy work and the development of various tools

The intended effect of the development contribution is based on the World Bank Group's "twin goals" to increase shared prosperity, and the eradication of extreme poverty. According to the theory of change, more and better jobs, increased trade flows and raised productivity, contribute to increased incomes and to achieve these goals. The World Bank Group (WBG) analysis underpinning this theory of change, identifies a number of challenges that limit the possibilities of achieving these goals. Examples of challenges include weak diversification, high transaction and trading costs, limited market access, and the poor being those who are hardest hit by trade shocks and exclusion.
The objective of the Umbrella Facility for Trade (UFT) is to provide support to developing countries towards integrating them in the global economy while increasing trade. It is based upon and supports the implementation of the World Banks Groups trade strategy which focuses on four main pillars: i) trade competitiveness and diversification ii) trade facilitation and transport logistics iii) market access and international trade cooperation and, iv) managing shocks and promoting greater inclusion.
Through a number of different activities at both the country and the global level, the World Bank Group contributes to creating more competitive and open markets, export diversification, reduce trading costs, strengthened capacity in policy making and, not least, an increased and upgraded participation in global value chains. Activities supported by the UFT include analyses and research, technical assistance, development of methods and tools, and the establishment of partnerships and dialogues.
The specific goals of the Umbrella Facility for Trade are to: increase the number of WBG projects that incorporate trade expand the testing, experimentation, research, and sharing of new ideas on trade gather, document, and disseminate results, data, and knowledge on trade related issues and increase the WBGs voice on global trade issues through enhanced global partnerships and engagements.
Through the UFT support is also channeled to the WBGs Trade Facilitation Support Programme (TFSP) which form an integral part of the contribution. Its objective is to improve cross border trade environments and support the full and effective implementation of the World Trade Organizations Trade Facilitation Agreement (WTO TFA).

description.narrative:
Since inception, 340 activities have been launched in over 120 countries with support from the UFT. FY24 (fiscal year 2024) included 24 new allocations to activities (totaling US$6 million for a total of US$57.5 million of allocated resources since program inception). (DOX 15/001180-270, Umbrella Facility for Trade Annual Report FY24, 2025, p. 9). Almost two thirds of the support has been directly allocated to country level work. (DOX 15/001180-274, Correspondence on shares to regions, 2025)
Achievements related to the specific goals of UFT
The UFT specifically seeks to leverage WBGs trade work in order to increase the number of WBG projects that incorporate trade expand the testing, experimentation, research, and sharing of new ideas on trade gather, document, and disseminate results, data, and knowledge on trade related issues and increase the WBGs voice on global trade issues through enhanced global partnerships and engagements.
Catalyzing World Bank lending to trade at country level: In FY24, UFT supported activities were directly informing US$5 billion of lending operations at the country/regional level (US$25 billion since the start of the program). (DOX 15/001180-270, Umbrella Facility for Trade Annual Report FY24, 2025, p. 10). For instance activities supported by TFSP informed the prior actions on trade facilitation in several country specific loans, including in Ukraine where the trade facilitation component supported amounted to USD 166 million. (DOX 15/001180-265, Trade Facilitation Support Program Annual Report FY 24, 2024, p. 31).
Leveraging of World Bank's own resources to support trade: Since the start of the program, 76 percent of UFT supported activities on trade were complemented by the World Banks own financial resources, totaling US$56.4 million, and thus nearly matching the donor contributions. (DOX 15/001180-270, Umbrella Facility for Trade Annual Report FY24, 2025, p. 10).
Incorporating gender into trade: The UFT also supports activities that aim to make trade more inclusive by assessing the potential impacts of changes in trade and trade policies for the poor as well as other marginalized groups. The annual target of 50% project spend on gender was again met in FY24. 12 grants specifically addressed gender issues, representing 61 percent of project implementation spend on gender. As an example, following the launch of the Trade Facilitation Challenges for Women Traders and Customs Brokers report, Brazil incorporated key recommendations into the National Trade Facilitation Committees Work Plan 2023-2025. (DOX 15/001180-270, Umbrella Facility for Trade Annual Report FY24, 2025, p. 10,77)
Climate/environment and trade: The World Bank advocates that promoting international trade and advancing sustainable economic development are not mutually exclusive and should be mutually reinforcing. In this context, the UFT is supporting work to review how trade and climate policies interact, and what actions governments can take to achieve harmony between trade and climate change mitigation and adaptation efforts. For instance, a CBAM Exposure Index was developed to help developing countries prepare and adjust to climate change regulations. In FY24, this tool was extended, and it now covers 120 countries. (DOX 15/001180-270, Umbrella Facility for Trade Annual Report FY24, 2025, p. 59,63). Together with the World Economic Forum and WTO the WB (with UFT support) also launched the Action on Climate and Trade Initiative (ACT) in FY 24. It aims to assist developing countries in analyzing issues that lie at the nexus of trade and climate change. Indonesia was the first country to be launched as part of the ACT initiative. Through ACT, the WBG, WTO and the World Economic Forum (WEF) engaged with public and private stakeholders in Indonesia to develop tailored analyses. Similar work was also undertaken in Rwanda and involved a work shop, in which the Swedish Embassy participated, with the aim to incorporate these aspects into the 2025 NDC and national adaptation plan updates. (DOX 15/001180-270, Umbrella Facility for Trade Annual Report FY24, 2025, p. 5051). Understanding and complying with the new EU deforestation regulation (EUDR) is another challenge for developing countries. In Peru UFT supported work guided the government to geolocate farmers that would be affected by the new regulation and craft a roadmap to ensure adherence to the EUDR, identifying key compliance gaps in Perus supply chains. (DOX 15/001180-270, Umbrella Facility for Trade Annual Report FY24, 2025, p. 24).
Achievements towards the four pillars of the WBG Trade Strategy
Pillar 1: Trade Competitiveness and Diversification
Pillar 1 aims to support domestic reforms for creating conducive policy environments for sustainable growth and creating more and better jobs by leveraging global trade opportunities. Under this pillar, the WBG helps governments to reap the gains from open trade, strengthen their market through diversification, and maximise their trade competitiveness by, for example, reviewing trade policies to remove biases about importing and exporting, and provide support to government interventions targeting specific market, policy, and institutional failures.
On an overall level 35 recommended laws, regulations, amendments/codes, and government policies were enacted /adopted which was slightly short of the previous target/FY 23 performance of 40. (DOX 15/001180-270, Umbrella Facility for Trade Annual Report FY24, 2025, p. 75).
Removing Tariffs: In Sri Lanka, UFT support encouraged foundational reforms to upgrade its trade policy framework. Support was provided to the drafting of the National Tariff Policy and phasing out of two paratariffs, namely the Port and Airport Levy and the Export Development Board Cess. In June 2024, a new National Tariff Policy was approved that will reduce average tariffs including bringing tariffs for intermediate goods and capital goods to below 10 percent in the next 3 years. The removal of tariffs is expected to increase the share of trade in Gross Domestic Product (GDP) from 41 percent (in 2021) to 45 percent (by 2025). (DOX 15/001180-270, Umbrella Facility for Trade Annual Report FY24, 2025, p. 12).
Supporting e-commerce: In the Philippines, with support from the UFT, the World Bank has helped support reforms, including the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the Internet Transactions Act (ITA). The ITA IRR outlines the essential procedures and guidelines for effective interagency collaboration, while also clearly defining the obligations and liabilities for digital platforms, e-marketplaces, e-retailers, online merchants, and online consumers. It includes the E-Commerce Philippine Trustmark, an online dispute resolution mechanism (B2B or B2C), and a Code of Conduct. DOX 15/001180-270, Umbrella Facility for Trade Annual Report FY24, 2025, p. 12).
Curbing Illicit Financial Flows (IFFs): UFT has supported research and given operational support in Niger, Nigeria, Kenya and Armenia with the aim to improve diagnostics of tariff evasion and to help policy makers curb IFFs. In Niger performance contracts were evaluated in order to improve their design. In Kenya the support helped identify risky traders, and in Nigeria a case study was used to foster dialogue on import bans. The approach is also informing policy dialogue in Armenia, where customs officials were trained in detecting customs fraud. The research was also presented at the World Customs Organisation's annual PICARD conference (an international platform to foster dialogue between customs administrations, academic communities and private sector) and at an expert workshop held by the International Anti-Corruption Academy in Vienna. DOX 15/001180-270, Umbrella Facility for Trade Annual Report FY24, 2025, p. 28-29).
Pillar 2: Trade Facilitation and Transport Logistics
Pillar 2 has the objective to ensure the efficient operation of border management processes as well as to reduce the costs of trade related transport, finance and logistics, and increase their timeliness and reliability.
Using Earth Observation (EO) and Artificial Intelligence (AI): In May 2024, the report Using Earth Observation and Artificial Intelligence to Survey Trade Supporting Activities and Infrastructure was published. Activities were carried out that examined how EO and AI is able to improve the fragmented data landscape in trade connectivity and logistics and inform policy reforms and WB lending operations. Indicators were built to measure border congestion and conveyance activity from space-borne sensors, and to inform the identification of interventions to ease the flow of goods at borders or other key nodes. Indicators were used to monitor the effects of disaster and time-sensitive events on trade nodes and to estimate border Green House Gases emissions. Policymakers will be able to use the tool to better inform policy design and improve the efficiency and physical integration of supply chains. For instance, the work can be directly used for corridor and infrastructure scoping and identification and, to improve physical accessibility, lastmile and intermodal readiness of existing or new colocated logistics facilities. DOX 15/001180-270, Umbrella Facility for Trade Annual Report FY24, 2025, p. 35).
Increasing alignment with WTO's Trade Facilitation Agreement (TFA): An external evaluation of TFSP assessed the program favorably, while identifying some shortcomings and recommendations that has been taken onboard by WB. Overall it stated that "The results of the Trade Facilitation Support Program suggest that the interventions have led to meaningful outcomes and impacts at a national and regional level" with reference to alignment with individual TFA measures for seven countries that was analyzed as part of the evaluation, using updated data since their baselines were collected. On average, alignment scores for these countries improved from 43% at baseline to 64%. DOX 15/001180-260, Trade Facilitation Support Programme Stocktaking & Learning Review Final Report, International Economics Consulting Ltd, 2024, p. 4).
Generating private sector savings through trade facilitation: By the end of FY24, it is estimated that TFSP supported activities have generated a total of USD 109 million in private sector savings (PSS) according to the applied methodology. For Sida partner countries this translates to USD 61 million in Ethiopia, USD 8 million in Liberia, USD 6 million in the Balkans, nearly USD 2 million in Zambia and about USD 1 million in Bangladesh. (DOX 15/001180-265, Trade Facilitation Support Program Annual Report FY 24, 2024, p. 29-30).
TFSP MENA-Window
The regional strategy for development cooperation with Middle East and North Africa delegated funds to GLOBEC to support expansion of a Trade Facilitation Support Program in the MENA-region, TFSP MENA, with a total of 77 MSEK, 2024-2026 covering eight countries. The World Bank TFSP Annual Report for 2024 was complemented by a separate Progress Report for TFSP MENA (DOX 15/001180-272).
TFSP MENA was officially launched at the WTO Aid for Trade Global Review in June 2024 and the majority of the activities were implemented between July and December 2024. The launch brought together both the World Bank Global Director for Trade and the Sweden´s Ambassador to WTO together with representatives from both the private sector (ICC) and government representatives from Yemen and Egypt as well as trade facilitation experts.
Activities started with Egypt, Jordan and Yemen and had a slow start in 2024, partly because the UFT were under transformation to the new UFT 2.0 which slowed down activities and partly due to challenges in the region. In Egypt the activities continued to build on the already started UK supported assistance to finalise an updated Time Release Study (TRS). The work included a review of import of sea cargo at major ports and one inland dry port. The TRS was finalized and discussed with the National Trade Facilitation Committee, NTFC and the Egyptian government. Workshop were held at NTFCs and the private sector to continue the dialogue under TFSP on TFA awareness, notification and measures needed to fulfil the agreement. Work on two critical documents was undertaken: Egypt National Trade Facilitation Strategy and Integrated Coordinated Risk Management Policy and Framework. (DOX 15/001180-272, Trade Facilitation Support Program in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, Progress Report July to December 2024, 2025, p. 13-14).
In Jordan work was undertaken to review the amendments to the Revised Customs Law (2024) to align with modern international standards, with particular focus on post clearance audit (PCA) regime and legal basis to implement the receipt of pre-arrival of cargo information to facilitate for traders. This work will also facilitate risk-based approach for border clearance and thus reducing time and need for physical inspections by Jordan Customs Department (JCD), which leads to reduced trading time and costs. This is strongly correlated also to improved investment climate and overall integration into global value chains. This TA work was leveraged into a lending operation from the World Bank Trust Fund Jordan Growth and Competitiveness DPO which contributes to sustainability and is an advantage of the UFT. (DOX 15/001180-272, Trade Facilitation Support Program in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, Progress Report July to December 2024, 2025, p. 16).
In Yemen, the TFSP MENA supported participation in WTO`s Committee Meetings on Trade Facilitation in October 2024 that allowed the Yemen delegation to learn about latest developments and WTO TFA implementation and LDC assistance. Moreover, WTO TFA implementation plan and ratification process was supported, and work done on drafting a TFA Roadmap and Action Plan. (DOX 15/001180-272, Trade Facilitation Support Program in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, Progress Report July to December 2024, 20-25, p. 7).
Pillar 3: Support for Market Access and International Trade Cooperation
The objective of this pillar is to reform trade policies that negatively impact developing countries, make international rules and institutions more supportive of the needs of developing countries, and evaluate what can be done to promote desirable integration and to protect the interests of those who are left out. Supporting WTO accession: The UFT has contributed to WTO accession processes including for fragile countries, helping them assess the pros and cons of WTO accession and its economic impacts. In FY 24 the WB provided guidance to Timor Leste on the process and on February 26 2024 at the 13th WTO Ministerial Conference their membership was approved. DOX 15/001180-270, Umbrella Facility for Trade Annual Report FY24, 2025, p. 38, 40).
Aiding Trade Negotiations: Kenya's Ministry of Trade & Industry requested support to prepare for negotiations on a Kenya-US Trade & Investment Strategic Partnership Agreement. 79 officials were trained on key issues over February 19-23, 2024, with an aim to equip kenyan negotiators with the necessary tools and knowledge to effectively navigate and enhancing its trade relationship with the US. DOX 15/001180-270, Umbrella Facility for Trade Annual Report FY24, 2025, p. 39).
Pillar 4: Managing Shocks and Promoting Greater Inclusion
Pillar 4 aims to address the reality of trade and to make distributional impacts of trade more visible, and the objective is to help policymakers understand the impacts and minimise adjustment costs and maximise benefits.
On an overall level the FY 24 reporting shows that previous years targets were met or exceeded, i.e 3 developing countries adopted national trade strategies which consider poverty reduction, and 9 countries used trade impacts assessments for Non-Tariff Measurements that address poverty/gender linkages. DOX 15/001180-270, Umbrella Facility for Trade Annual Report FY24, 2025, p. 77).
Informing the Ukraine Plan 2024-2027: a comprehensive monitoring effort to uncover the impact of the Russian invasion on the private sector in Ukraine was conducted. In particular, the activity deployed a variety of new tools to provide different perspectives on the impacts on firms within the context of the ongoing conflict. These tools included an in-country Business Pulse Survey of over 2,700 firms, a multinational corporation survey, and an innovative analysis of real time data on economic activity across multiple locations relying on satellite imagery data. Analytical work informed the WB's advice to the Government of Ukraine in the design of the Ukraine Plan 2024-2027, and in setting the business environment reform priorities of the Ukraine Reform Matrix 20242027. The Ukraine Plan 2024-2027 is co-financed by a dedicated EU support mechanism providing up to €50 billion for Ukraine's recovery, reconstruction, and modernization efforts between 2024 and 2027. The Ukraine Reforms Matrix 2024-2027 is a new analytical tool to support effective decision making and management of the reform process. DOX 15/001180-270, Umbrella Facility for Trade Annual Report FY24, 2025, p. 47-48).
Leveraging Trade for More and Better Jobs: In FY24, with support from UFT, the WB published a Trade and Jobs flagship report, which was released in September. On September 10, 2024, the report was presented at the WTO Public Forum. The reports main conclusions are that increased trade has been associated with more and better jobs over the last three decades. Not only has trade created more jobs but it has done so especially for women. It has also led to higher labor earnings on average as well as reduced wage inequality. And trade has been tied to more productive and salaried employment. However, the analyses also provide support for some concerns. Unlike middle-income countries, trade in low-income countries does not seem to create large numbers of jobs or reduce wage inequality significantly. Moreover, the positive effects from trade have become weaker after the Global Financial Crisis. One key takeaway is that there is a need to strengthen the global rules-based system supporting trade. While the report has a global focus, the new data and tools have already been applied to specific countries. Trade and jobs assessments have been undertaken so far in a Viet Nam 2045 Global Value Chain (GVS) report green industrial policy and GVCs reports for Bulgaria, Croatia, Poland, and Romania, and an India report on linking MSMEs to global markets. DOX 15/001180-270, Umbrella Facility for Trade Annual Report FY24, 2025, p. 48-49).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
